Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to velvety dark spots on leaves with indistinct margins; leaves yellow and drop prematurely; scabby rough lesions on fruit.
organic_remedies: Spray wettable sulfur or copper hydroxide before bloom and immediately after rain periods.
Apply potassium bicarbonate (0.5% concentration) to raise leaf surface pH and inhibit spore germination.
Spray fermented horsetail (Equisetum arvense) extract rich in natural silica to strengthen leaf cuticles.
chemical_remedies: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5 g/L during primary bud break and pre-pink stage.
Rotate with Difenoconazole 25% EC at 0.5 mL/L or Kresoxim-methyl 44.3% SC at 0.6 mL/L during active shoot growth.
Observe a strict 28-day pre-harvest interval (PHI) for systemic fungicides.
preventive_practices: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn or apply 5% urea spray to speed leaf decomposition and destroy overwintering perithecia.
Prune the tree canopy in late winter to facilitate rapid leaf drying and sunlight penetration.
Plant scab-resistant cultivars such as Liberty, Prima, or Enterprise.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Small purple spots on leaves expanding into 'frogeye' spots with brown centers and purple borders; cankers on twigs; firm black rot on fruit.
organic_remedies: Apply Bordeaux mixture (4-4-50) or copper sulfate spray during the dormant stage.
Prune and burn infected twigs, mummified fruits, and dead wood where pycnidia overwinter.
Bio-fungicide drench with Bacillus subtilis (Serenade ASO) at 5 mL/L during bloom.
chemical_remedies: Apply Captan 50% WP at 2.0 g/L or Thiophanate-methyl 70% WP at 1.0 g/L.
Apply Pyraclostrobin + Boscalid (Pristine WG) during petal fall at recommended label rates.
Re-spray every 10 to 14 days if wet weather persists.
preventive_practices: Cut out cankers at least 15 cm below infected margins using sterilized shears (disinfected in 70% isopropyl alcohol).
Prevent mechanical wounds, frost cracking, and sunscald on tree bark.
Remove fire blight strikes and dead branches which serve as fungal reservoir sites.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange circular lesions on upper leaf surfaces; later developing raised tubular fungal cups (aecia) on the underside.
organic_remedies: Apply liquid sulfur sprays every 7-10 days from pink bud through petal fall.
Use copper soap or copper octanoate as a protective bio-pesticide early in the season.
Inspect and manually prune cedar galls from nearby Eastern red cedar junipers in winter.
chemical_remedies: Apply Myclobutanil 10% WP at 1.0 g/L or Triadimefon 25% WP at 0.5 g/L.
Apply Mancozeb 75% WP protectant at early vegetative emergence.
Do not apply systemic triazoles more than 3 times per season to prevent pathogen resistance.
preventive_practices: Remove surrounding red cedar and juniper hosts within a 500-meter radius if possible.
Select rust-resistant apple varieties like Gala, Honeycrisp, or William's Pride.
Maintain adequate nitrogen balance to avoid overly succulent shoot susceptibility.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green leaves with clean margins, no necrotic lesions, fungal sporulation, or chlorotic mottling.
organic_remedies: Maintain preventative compost mulch around root dripline (avoiding trunk contact).
Foliar spray with seaweed extract (2 mL/L) to boost natural systemic acquired resistance (SAR).
chemical_remedies: No chemical fungicides or bactericides required. Continue regular scouting.
preventive_practices: Maintain regular drip irrigation and annual soil fertility testing.
Keep orchard floor mowed and clear of decomposing plant debris.

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Deep green glossy leaves, sturdy canes, and uniform vigor with zero stem blight or rust spots.
organic_remedies: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5 - 5.2) using elemental sulfur and organic pine bark mulch.
Apply kelp meal and fish hydrolysate during spring flush.
chemical_remedies: No chemical interventions required.
preventive_practices: Ensure drip irrigation to prevent crown rot (Phytophthora cinnamomi).
Annual winter pruning to remove weak and crossing canes.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery circular patches of mycelium on young leaves and succulent shoots; leaves curl upward and blister.
organic_remedies: Spray horticultural mineral oil (1% emulsion) or neem oil (5 mL/L) at first sign of white mycelium.
Apply wettable sulfur at 3 g/L during vegetative growth (avoid if temperatures exceed 32°C).
Potassium silicate foliar spray to fortify epidermal cell walls.
chemical_remedies: Apply Tebuconazole 25.9% EC at 0.75 mL/L or Trifloxystrobin 50% WG at 0.3 g/L.
Apply Azoxystrobin 23% SC at 1.0 mL/L in rotation with sterol inhibitors.
Spray every 10 to 14 days while new vegetative flushes emerge.
preventive_practices: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which produces excessively succulent growth.
Prune interior canopy shoots to improve cross-ventilation and sunlight penetration.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.

weather_triggers.leaf_wetness_hours: Dry leaves with high ambient humidity

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: Lush green, intact cherry leaves with smooth margins and no leaf curl or shot-hole perforations.
organic_remedies: Apply well-decomposed organic manure and mycorrhizal inoculants around drip line.
chemical_remedies: No chemical treatments needed.
preventive_practices: Monitor bi-weekly for black cherry aphids and cherry fruit flies.
Maintain drip irrigation schedule and weed-free tree basins.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Small, tan necrotic spots with chlorotic halos that expand into long, narrow rectangular lesions restricted by leaf veins.
organic_remedies: Apply foliar sprays of Trichoderma harzianum bio-fungicide at 5 g/L during early vegetative stages (V6-V8).
Incorporate bio-char and diverse crop compost into the soil to accelerate residue decomposition.
chemical_remedies: Spray Pyraclostrobin + Fluxapyroxad (Priaxor) at recommended label rate during VT to R1 (tasseling to silking).
Apply Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole at 1.0 mL/L if disease reaches ear leaf prior to tasseling.
Ensure application timing protects the ear leaf and top three leaves.
preventive_practices: Practice strict 2-year crop rotation with non-host crops like soybean, alfalfa, or oats.
Utilize conservation tillage or deep plowing to bury infested corn stubble.
Select corn hybrids with high GLS resistance ratings.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Golden brown to cinnamon-brown powdery pustules (uredinia) scattered across both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
organic_remedies: Spray wettable sulfur at 3 g/L or potassium bicarbonate at early symptom appearance.
Foliar spray with Bacillus amyloliquefaciens strain D747.
chemical_remedies: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5 g/L or Propiconazole 25% EC at 1.0 mL/L.
Spray Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC at 1.0 mL/L if pustules appear before silking on susceptible hybrids.
preventive_practices: Plant rust-resistant hybrids carrying Rp genes.
Plant early in the season to allow crops to mature before high rust spore loads arrive on southerly winds.
Maintain balanced soil phosphorus and potassium.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Large, cigar-shaped, grayish-green to tan lesions (2.5 to 15 cm long) with smooth margins, often coalescing to scorch entire leaves.
organic_remedies: Foliar bio-control spray with Bacillus subtilis or Pseudomonas fluorescens at 5 mL/L.
Apply copper octanoate (soap) at vegetative stage V6.
chemical_remedies: Apply Propiconazole 13.9% + Difenoconazole 13.9% at 1.0 mL/L or Azoxystrobin 23% SC at 1.0 mL/L.
Apply Pyraclostrobin at 1.25 L/ha when lesion threshold reaches 1 lesion per leaf prior to silking.
Ensure thorough spray coverage of the upper canopy.
preventive_practices: Plant NCLB-resistant hybrid corn containing Ht1, Ht2, or Ht3 resistance genes.
Tillage management to bury crop debris where conidia overwinter.
Rotate out of corn for at least 1-2 seasons.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Broad, vibrant deep-green leaves free of rust pustules, rectangular lesions, or wilting margins.
organic_remedies: Maintain side-dressing of vermicompost and bio-fertilizers (Azotobacter & PSB).
chemical_remedies: No chemical fungicides necessary.
preventive_practices: Ensure timely weed management in first 35 days (critical weed-free period).
Regular scouting for armyworm and stem borer egg masses.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Small reddish-brown circular spots on leaves with black margins and tiny black fruiting bodies (pycnidia); berries shrivel into hard black mummies.
organic_remedies: Spray copper sulfate / hydrated lime (Bordeaux mixture 3-3-50) from bud break to veraison.
Apply potassium bicarbonate and sulfur alternately during vegetative flush.
Prune and destroy all mummified fruit clusters hanging on the vines or resting on the soil.
chemical_remedies: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5 g/L or Myclobutanil 10% WP at 1.0 g/L.
Apply Kresoxim-methyl 44.3% SC at 0.7 mL/L or Difenoconazole 25% EC at 0.5 mL/L.
Critical spray window is immediate pre-bloom through 4 weeks post-bloom.
preventive_practices: Canopy shoot thinning and leaf pulling around fruit zone to maximize wind airflow and sunlight.
Maintain clean vineyard floor by disking or mulching over overwintered mummies.
Plant less susceptible cultivars (e.g., Norton or Chancellor).

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' interveinal chlorosis and necrosis on leaves; purple or brown speckling on berries; vascular wood necrosis inside cane wood.
organic_remedies: Apply Trichoderma atroviride pruning wound sealant immediately after winter pruning.
Spray copper oxychloride to protect freshly cut vines from airborne basidiospores.
No curative chemical exists; diseased vines require surgical trunk renewal.
chemical_remedies: Paint large pruning cuts with Thiophanate-methyl or pyraclostrobin-based wound dressings within 24 hours of cutting.
Foliar application of phosphite-based systemic elicitors to slow decline.
preventive_practices: Delay pruning until late in the dormant season (February/March) when wound healing is rapid.
Sterilize pruning shears between vines with 70% ethanol or 10% household bleach.
Uproot and burn severely decayed vines showing apoplexy (sudden vine collapse).

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown to black necrotic spots with halos on older leaves; premature defoliation leading to exposed sunburnt fruit.
organic_remedies: Spray copper hydroxide (Kocide) at 2.0 g/L or Bordeaux mixture (1%) after harvest.
Apply biological biocontrol agent Bacillus subtilis (Serenade) at 4 mL/L.
chemical_remedies: Apply Carbendazim 50% WP at 1.0 g/L or Thiophanate Methyl 70% WP at 1.0 g/L.
Spray Azoxystrobin 23% SC at 1.0 mL/L or Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5 g/L upon initial leaf spotting.
preventive_practices: Remove and burn leaf litter following autumn senescence.
Ensure proper trellis shoot positioning to prevent dense, trapped moisture canopies.
Maintain adequate potassium nutrition to fortify leaf cell membranes.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Broad, vibrant dark-green grape leaves with healthy lobed margins and no spotting, powdery coating, or necrosis.
organic_remedies: Apply balanced compost teas and organic mycorrhizal inoculants.
Maintain foliar calcium and boron sprays during pre-bloom to enhance fruit set.
chemical_remedies: No chemical interventions required.
preventive_practices: Routine canopy management (shoot tucking, suckering, and leaf pulling).
Soil moisture monitoring using tensiometers to avoid waterlogging.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).pathogen: Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (Bacteria vectored by Asian Citrus Psyllid)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Asymmetrical blotchy mottle chlorosis on leaves; yellow shoots; small, misshapen, lopsided fruit that stays green at base and tastes bitter.
organic_remedies: Release natural biological control predator wasps (Tamarixia radiata) to parasitize citrus psyllid nymphs.
Apply high-grade horticultural narrow-range petroleum oils (1-2%) to suffocate adult psyllids and prevent egg laying.
Intensive foliar nutritional therapy (Zinc, Manganese, Iron chelate, Boron, Potassium) to prolong tree productivity.
chemical_remedies: Control psyllid vectors with Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (soil drench) or Thiamethoxam 25% WG at 0.3 g/L.
Rotate with Dimethoate 30% EC or Chlorpyrifos during seasonal vegetative flush cycles.
Strict quarantine compliance: antibiotics (oxytetracycline injections) only where federally authorized.
preventive_practices: Plant only certified disease-free grafted saplings from screenhouse nurseries.
Eradicate infected trees promptly to eliminate bacterial inocula for surrounding orchards.
Install yellow sticky traps to continuously monitor psyllid flight.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Angular, water-soaked purple-brown lesions on leaves that drop out creating a 'shot-hole' appearance; deep pitted cracks on fruit.
organic_remedies: Spray copper sulfate or copper octanoate during dormant season and post-harvest defoliation.
Apply Bacillus subtilis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens biocontrol formulations during early petal fall.
Use zinc sulfate foliar sprays in autumn to facilitate timely leaf drop.
chemical_remedies: Apply Oxytetracycline (Mycoshield) at 1.5 g/L starting at petal fall through shuck split.
Low-rate fixed copper sprays (Copper hydroxide at 0.5 g/L) with hydrated lime to minimize phytotoxicity.
Do not apply copper during high heat or slow drying conditions to prevent severe leaf scorch.
preventive_practices: Plant resistant peach varieties like Candor, Dixired, Sentinel, or Redhaven.
Avoid orchard sites exposed to severe sandy wind abrasion which creates bacterial entry wounds.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.

Peach___healthy.symptoms: Long, lanceolate, glossy green leaves without shot-hole perforations, leaf curl, or gumming lesions.
organic_remedies: Maintain organic tree basin mulching with wood chips and compost.
chemical_remedies: No chemical sprays required.
preventive_practices: Apply standard dormant copper spray in late winter to prevent Taphrina deformans (Peach Leaf Curl).
Scout for peach tree borers around lower crown.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Water-soaked, circular-to-irregular dark brown spots with yellow halos on leaves; leaves turn yellow and drop; blistered scabs on pepper fruit.
organic_remedies: Spray copper hydroxide + Bacillus subtilis (Serenade) at 4 mL/L every 7 days.
Hot-water seed treatment at 50°C for 25 minutes prior to nursery sowing.
Foliar spray with biological systemic acquired resistance (SAR) inducers like chitosan.
chemical_remedies: Apply Streptomycin sulfate (9%) + Tetracycline hydrochloride (1%) at 0.5 g/L (where registered).
Tank mix Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (2.5 g/L) with Mancozeb 75% WP (2.0 g/L) to overcome copper-tolerant bacterial strains.
Reapply after every heavy rain.
preventive_practices: Use certified disease-free, pepper-spot resistant seed hybrids.
Strict 2 to 3-year crop rotation away from solanaceous crops (tomato, potato, eggplant).
Avoid working in or harvesting pepper fields while foliage is wet.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Glossy, uniform emerald-green foliage with vigorous terminal growth and no chlorosis, wilting, or necrotic spots.
organic_remedies: Top-dress with vermicompost and potassium-rich bio-extracts.
chemical_remedies: No chemical sprays required.
preventive_practices: Maintain consistent drip fertigation to avoid blossom end rot (calcium deficiency).
Install reflective silver mulches to repel thrips and aphids.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Characteristic dark brown, concentric ring lesions ('target-board' pattern) surrounded by chlorotic yellow halo on older lower leaves.
organic_remedies: Apply copper sulfate or copper soap (0.5%) at first symptom detection.
Bio-fungicide foliar spray with Trichoderma harzianum or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens at 5 g/L.
Foliar spray with neem oil extract (10,000 ppm) at 3 mL/L.
chemical_remedies: Apply Chlorothalonil 75% WP at 2.0 g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5 g/L as protectants.
For curative systemic action, apply Azoxystrobin 23% SC at 1.0 mL/L or Difenoconazole 25% EC at 0.5 mL/L.
Alternate FRAC groups to prevent strobilurin resistance.
preventive_practices: Ensure balanced nitrogen fertilization; avoid nutrient stress during tuber bulking.
Maintain drip irrigation; do not irrigate in late afternoon or evening.
Allow 3-year crop rotation between potato and other nightshade crops.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale-green to dark brown lesions that rapidly turn black; delicate white fungal mold on leaf undersides in high humidity; tuber rot.
organic_remedies: Spray copper hydroxide (Kocide 3000) at 2.0 g/L prior to rain events.
Bio-pesticide spray with Bacillus subtilis at 5 mL/L.
Destroy and bag all infected plants immediately to prevent airborne sporangia spread.
chemical_remedies: Apply Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Curzate) at 2.5 g/L or Dimethomorph 50% WP at 1.0 g/L.
Apply Metalaxyl-M 4% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Ridomil Gold) at 2.5 g/L at disease outbreak.
Mandatory spray interval: 5 to 7 days during cool, rainy, fog-heavy periods.
preventive_practices: Plant only certified pathogen-free seed tubers.
Hilling/ridging soil adequately around stems to protect shallow tubers from rain-washed zoospores.
Kill potato vine foliage (desiccation) 2 weeks before harvest.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Lush, dark-green canopy, sturdy stems, upright posture with zero water-soaked spots, target rings, or wilting.
organic_remedies: Foliar spray with sea kelp extract (2 mL/L) to strengthen plant stress tolerance.
Ensure sufficient potassium sulfate soil application.
chemical_remedies: No chemical sprays needed.
preventive_practices: Monitor fields with potato late blight forecasting tools.
Regular scouting for Colorado potato beetle and potato leafhopper.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Vigorous serrated compound leaves with vivid green coloration, sturdy primocanes, and zero rust pustules or powdery mildew.
organic_remedies: Mulch root zone with organic sawdust or wood chips to preserve root moisture.
Apply balanced organic compost.
chemical_remedies: No chemicals required.
preventive_practices: Trellis canes to maintain upright air circulation.
Remove dead floricanes immediately after fruiting.

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Trifoliate leaves exhibiting healthy, uniform green coloration, robust nodulation at root crown, and zero frogeye spots.
organic_remedies: Inoculate seeds with Bradyrhizobium japonicum to maximize biological nitrogen fixation.
chemical_remedies: No chemicals needed.
preventive_practices: Regular scouting for soybean aphid and pod borer.
Maintain weed canopy control in early growth stages.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: Talcum powder-like white fungal growth covering upper and lower surfaces of leaves and stems; leaves turn yellow, brown, and become brittle.
organic_remedies: Apply potassium bicarbonate (5 g/L) + horticultural oil (5 mL/L) to rapidly destroy fungal hyphae.
Spray 40% cow milk / 60% water solution in direct sunlight; lactoferrin generates antiseptic free radicals.
Neem oil (cold-pressed) at 5 mL/L with mild dish soap emulsifier.
chemical_remedies: Apply Myclobutanil 10% WP at 1.0 g/L or Triflumizole at labeled rates.
Apply Azoxystrobin 23% SC at 1.0 mL/L or Cyflufenamid 5% EW at 0.5 mL/L.
Begin fungicide applications at first sighting of colonies on lower leaf undersides.
preventive_practices: Plant resistant cucurbit varieties (labeled PMR).
Provide generous spacing (at least 90 cm between plants) to minimize humidity stagnation.
Drip irrigate only; avoid wetting sprawling leaves.

weather_triggers.leaf_wetness_hours: Dry leaves with humid shaded microclimate

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Numerous small, dark purple or reddish irregular blotches on leaves; centers do not turn white; severe lesions cause leaves to curl, brown, and scorch.
organic_remedies: Apply copper sulfate or copper octanoate (soap) at early spring crown emergence.
Spray bio-fungicide Bacillus amyloliquefaciens at 4 mL/L.
Prune and destroy heavily blighted leaves after the harvest renovation period.
chemical_remedies: Apply Captan 50% WP at 2.0 g/L or Thiophanate-methyl 70% WP at 1.0 g/L.
Apply Azoxystrobin 23% SC at 1.0 mL/L or Pyraclostrobin 20% WG at 0.8 g/L.
Re-treat every 10-14 days during wet spring flushes.
preventive_practices: Plant on raised beds covered with straw mulch or black plastic to prevent soil splash.
Use certified disease-free strawberry runner plants.
Mow and renovate June-bearing fields immediately following last harvest.

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Tri-foliate, bright emerald-green leaves with crisp serrations, robust crown vigor, and zero necrotic blotches.
organic_remedies: Side-dress with well-rotted compost and bone meal for phosphorus.
chemical_remedies: No chemical sprays needed.
preventive_practices: Maintain clean straw mulch to keep berries and lower foliage off wet soil.
Monitor for two-spotted spider mites on leaf undersides.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small (less than 3 mm), dark brown water-soaked circular lesions with chlorotic halos; lesions coalesce causing general defoliation; scab-like spots on green tomatoes.
organic_remedies: Apply Copper octanoate / Copper Hydroxide (2 g/L) + Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (3 g/L).
Pre-soak tomato seeds in hot water (50°C for 25 minutes) or 1.3% sodium hypochlorite solution.
Spray bacteriophage biological formulations (AgriPhage) specific to Xanthomonas.
chemical_remedies: Tank mix Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (2.5 g/L) with Mancozeb 75% WP (2.0 g/L) to inactivate copper-tolerant bacterial populations.
Apply Kasugamycin 3% SL at 1.5 mL/L or Streptomycin formulations where legally registered.
Avoid spraying during high humidity to minimize leaf surface wetness duration.
preventive_practices: Never use overhead sprinkler irrigation; always use drip tape underneath plastic mulch.
Do not enter, prune, or stake tomato plants while leaves are wet from dew or rain.
Perform minimum 2-year crop rotation away from solanaceous crops.

weather_triggers.leaf_wetness_hours: Heavy driving rain or prolonged overhead wetting

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown to black necrotic spots with distinct concentric rings ('bullseye' / target pattern) surrounded by yellow chlorosis, starting on lower older leaves.
organic_remedies: Apply Copper Hydroxide (Kocide) at 2.0 g/L or Bordeaux mixture (1%) at first sign.
Foliar spray with Trichoderma viride or Bacillus subtilis at 5 mL/L.
Strip off the lowest 30 cm of tomato foliage once plants reach 1 meter to prevent soil splash inoculation.
chemical_remedies: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP at 2.0 g/L at early vegetative stage.
Apply Azoxystrobin 23% SC at 1.0 mL/L or Difenoconazole 25% EC at 0.5 mL/L when lesions appear.
Spray every 7 to 10 days during warm, humid weather.
preventive_practices: Stake and cage tomato plants securely to keep foliage off ground level.
Apply 5-8 cm of clean organic straw mulch around plant base.
Rotate out of solanaceous crops for 3 consecutive years.

weather_triggers.leaf_wetness_hours: Alternating wet and dry humid cycles

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular greasy water-soaked pale greenish-black lesions on leaves and petioles; white fuzzy sporulation on leaf undersides in high humidity; stems turn brown and collapse.
organic_remedies: Spray copper sulfate or copper hydroxide protectant (2.5 g/L) before forecast rain periods.
Bio-fungicide spray with Bacillus subtilis (Serenade) at 5 mL/L.
Immediately cull and destroy infected plants; do not compost in home compost piles.
chemical_remedies: Apply Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP at 2.5 g/L or Dimethomorph 50% WP at 1.0 g/L.
Apply Metalaxyl-M 4% + Mancozeb 64% WP at 2.5 g/L at first disease report in the district.
Spray interval must be tightened to 5 days during persistent cool, rainy, overcast weather.
preventive_practices: Plant late blight-resistant varieties (e.g., Mountain Magic, Defiant PHR, Plum Regal).
Ensure wide plant spacing (60-90 cm) for maximum canopy airflow.
Never compost late-blight infected foliage or fruit.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow or light-green spots with indistinct margins on upper leaf surface; olive-green to brownish velvety mold growth on the corresponding underside.
organic_remedies: Apply copper octanoate (copper soap) or wettable sulfur (2 g/L) on leaf undersides.
Bio-control spray with Bacillus subtilis at 4 mL/L.
Prune lower older leaves to open up dense lower canopy in greenhouse environments.
chemical_remedies: Apply Chlorothalonil 75% WP at 2.0 g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5 g/L.
Apply Difenoconazole 25% EC at 0.5 mL/L or Boscalid + Pyraclostrobin.
Ensure spray nozzles target the undersides of the leaves where sporulation occurs.
preventive_practices: Maintain greenhouse or tunnel relative humidity strictly below 85% with exhaust fans.
Heat and ventilate greenhouse at dusk to prevent condensation on foliage.
Plant resistant tomato cultivars with Cf resistance genes.

weather_triggers.leaf_wetness_hours: High relative humidity in still air

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small, circular spots (2-3 mm) with dark brown borders and distinctly gray or tan centers containing tiny black specks (pycnidia); leaves turn yellow and drop.
organic_remedies: Apply fixed copper fungicide (copper hydroxide) at 2.0 g/L every 7-10 days.
Foliar spray with Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide (4 g/L).
Prune off infected lower leaves immediately upon appearance.
chemical_remedies: Apply Chlorothalonil 75% WP at 2.0 g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5 g/L as protective sprays.
Apply Azoxystrobin 23% SC at 1.0 mL/L or Pyraclostrobin at label rate.
Begin fungicide applications early before disease spreads to the upper third of the plant.
preventive_practices: Apply heavy straw or plastic mulch to create a barrier against soil-borne fungal spores.
Strict weed control to eliminate solanaceous weed hosts (horse nettle, black nightshade).
Clean garden debris thoroughly in autumn and practice 3-year crop rotation.

weather_triggers.leaf_wetness_hours: 48 hours of wet weather or frequent rain

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow or white stippling on upper leaf surfaces; bronze or scorched appearance; fine delicate webbing on leaf undersides and terminal shoots.
organic_remedies: Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis or Neoseiulus californicus) at 5-10 per m².
Spray cold-pressed neem oil (5 mL/L) or potassium salts of fatty acids (insecticidal soap) at 10 mL/L.
Spray rosemary oil or thyme oil-based botanical miticides.
chemical_remedies: Apply Spiromesifen 22.9% SC at 1.0 mL/L or Abamectin 1.9% EC at 0.5 mL/L.
Apply Fenpyroximate 5% EC at 1.0 mL/L or Bifenazate 24% SC at 0.75 mL/L.
Always rotate acaricide chemical modes of action; mites develop resistance rapidly.
preventive_practices: Avoid broad-spectrum synthetic pyrethroid sprays which kill beneficial predator mites.
Maintain adequate irrigation; drought-stressed plants are preferred mite hosts.
Hose down dusty field perimeters to reduce dust-facilitated mite outbreaks.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Pinpoint brown lesions with yellow halos expanding into circular necrotic spots with light brown centers and faint concentric zones; fruit develops sunken lesions.
organic_remedies: Apply copper hydroxide + Bacillus subtilis bio-fungicide at 4 g/L.
Prune dense lower foliage to facilitate rapid air exchange and light penetration.
Spray potassium bicarbonate at 5 g/L.
chemical_remedies: Apply Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole at 1.0 mL/L or Fluxapyroxad + Pyraclostrobin.
Apply Chlorothalonil 75% WP at 2.0 g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5 g/L as preventive cover.
Maintain 7 to 10 day spray cycle during rainy tropical periods.
preventive_practices: Ensure proper row orientation with prevailing wind for canopy ventilation.
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization.
Deep plow crop residues immediately after final harvest.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe upward cupping and curling of leaf margins; stunted chlorotic leaves with mottled yellowing; bushy upright plant dwarfism; complete fruit drop.
organic_remedies: Install yellow sticky cards (1 trap per 100 m²) to trap adult whiteflies.
Spray cold-pressed neem oil (10,000 ppm) at 3 mL/L or Beauveria bassiana entomopathogenic fungus at 5 g/L.
Cover young nursery beds with 50-mesh insect-proof screening.
chemical_remedies: No direct chemical antiviral cure exists for infected plants; control vector whitefly.
Apply Dinotefuran 20% SG at 0.5 g/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG at 0.3 g/L.
Apply Pyriproxyfen 10% EC at 1.0 mL/L (insect growth regulator) to break whitefly reproduction.
preventive_practices: Plant TYLCV-resistant hybrids with Ty-1, Ty-2, or Ty-3 resistance genes.
Use UV-reflective silver plastic mulches to deter landing whiteflies.
Rogue out and bury virus-infected plants immediately to prevent field-wide vector spread.

weather_triggers.leaf_wetness_hours: Dry, warm seasons favor whitefly population explosions

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves; blistered, distorted or strap-like 'shoestring' leaves; internal brown necrosis in fruit wall.
organic_remedies: Soak seeds in 10% trisodium phosphate (TSP) solution for 30 minutes before sowing.
Disinfect hands and pruning tools in non-fat dry skim milk (20% solution) to neutralize virus particles.
Destroy and safely bury infected plants; do not leave residues on soil surface.
chemical_remedies: No chemical viricides exist. Control relies entirely on sanitation and genetic resistance.
Spray chitosan or acibenzolar-S-methyl (Actigard) as systemic acquired resistance (SAR) elicitors on surrounding healthy crops.
preventive_practices: Plant tobacco/tomato mosaic virus-resistant cultivars carrying Tm-2 or Tm-2^2 genes.
Strict worker hygiene: no tobacco smoking or chewing near tomato fields (tobacco carries mosaic virus).
Wash all stakes, cages, and nursery trays with 10% bleach before reuse.

weather_triggers.leaf_wetness_hours: Mechanically spread by touch, pruning, and wind brushing

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Vigorous, dark-green compound foliage with strong terminal growth, sturdy stems, and no chlorotic spotting or leaf curl.
organic_remedies: Top-dress with well-cured compost and liquid vermiwash (50 mL/L).
Spray seaweed extract (2 mL/L) every 14 days during flowering to boost fruit set.
chemical_remedies: No chemicals required.
preventive_practices: Maintain consistent drip irrigation to avoid fruit cracking and blossom end rot.
Ensure proper staking and bottom pruning to maintain airflow.
